# AI agent beliefs and manager decisions

Package for the five-article agent-belief study. It contains the original and altered training materials, the frozen Mistral Participant Agent Interaction records, the trained Mistral and Qwen adapter lineage, and the implementation of the base manager procedure.

**Scope.** This package implements the base prompts and records the responses generated by that procedure. This implementation is for new base-procedure runs.

## Contents

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `DATA` | Five article sets: 25 clean Word versions, 20 genuine tracked-change Word versions, 25 exact training texts, the frozen 20 Participant Agent Interaction records, questions and source-bound answer keys. |
| `Models` | Pinned base-model manifests, tokenizer/configuration files, adapter configuration and checksum manifests, and 200 manager-instance definitions for each family. Safetensors are distributed through the private release. |
| `Training logs` | Retained per-step training losses, validation/selection records, training examples and lineage. |
| `Parallel Agent Setup` | One-base/multiple-LoRA vLLM server, bounded asynchronous client, token accounting and per-instance timings. |
| `Experiment Codes` | Base-prompt Experiments 1a–3a (Mistral) and 1b–3b (Qwen), optional unaided recall checks, Participant Agent Interaction procedure, training entrypoints and notebooks. |
| [Results & Analysis Codes (Appendix B)](Results%20%26%20Analysis%20Codes%20%28Appendix%20B%29/README.md) | One combined runner and eleven exhibit scripts for the final Appendix B tables and figures, with dependencies and placeholder input manifests. Final analysis data are not included. |

## Full running code

Open [Experiment Codes: scripts and complete-code notebooks](Experiment%20Codes/README.md) for the six Mistral/Qwen experiment entrypoints. Each experiment folder contains a matching entrypoint (for example, `Experiment_1a/run_experiment_1a.py` or `Experiment_1b/run_experiment_1b.py`), a complete-code notebook, exact prompt, settings and run instructions.

The [Participant Agent Interaction runner](Experiment%20Codes/Mistral/Participant_Agent_Interaction/README.md) has separate prepare, advance, review, status and export commands. Its notebook displays the complete interaction implementation. The manager notebooks similarly display all shared code, rather than hiding the implementation behind an import.

## Models and assignments

| Family | Base model | Pinned revision | Inference context cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mistral | `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2` | `b70aa86578567ba3301b21c8a27bea4e8f6d6d61` | 16,384 tokens |
| Qwen | `Qwen/Qwen-7B-Chat` | `218aa3240fd5a5d1e80bb6c47d5d774361913706` | 16,384 tokens |

These are the caps of the configured experiment servers, including the output reservation; they should not be confused with a claim about a model's maximum architectural context.

| Agent or manager | Its five assigned articles | Pair question |
|---|---|---|
| A | Original versions | Participates in every pair |
| B | Magnitude alterations | A–B: magnitude |
| C | Actor alterations | A–C: actor |
| D | Mechanism alterations | A–D: mechanism |
| E | All three alterations | A–E: all three components |

There are five learned manager adapters per family. Each of the 200 instance definitions starts with an empty conversation and references one immutable adapter. An instance is a request context, not a separately trained weight set.

## Run order

1. Clone the private repository. Replace `YOUR PATHWAY` in notebook setup cells with the clone directory, or open the notebooks from within the clone so the root is discovered automatically.
2. Restore the base files and adapter archives using `tools/fetch_models.py`; see `Models/README.md`. Verify their hashes before GPU use.
3. Create the dedicated vLLM environment using `Parallel Agent Setup/README.md`. Start only one model family at a time.
4. Open `Parallel Agent Setup/notebooks/00_Setup.ipynb`, then `Experiment Codes/notebooks/01_Spawn_Agents.ipynb`.
5. Use the frozen Participant Agent Interaction records as the manager inputs. The separate `02_Participant_Agent_Interaction.ipynb` notebook and the complete-code notebook in the participant folder expose the procedure for a new interaction run, including its semantic stopping review.
6. Optionally run the unaided recall check notebook. It asks only a question, preserves every first response and leaves semantic scoring explicit; it does not provide articles or replace answers.
7. Prepare and inspect all exact inputs in `04_Manager_Experiments.ipynb`. Set its execution switch only when ready to generate a new batch. Run Experiments 1a, 2a and 3a (Mistral), or 1b, 2b and 3b (Qwen) in sequence for the selected family, then switch servers for the other family.
8. After obtaining the data for all six experiments, prepare the final workbooks, reviewed coding files and input manifests using the schema in [Results & Analysis Codes (Appendix B)](Results%20%26%20Analysis%20Codes%20%28Appendix%20B%29/README.md). Install its pinned requirements, then run `Complete_Run_Code.py` with your local `--inputs`, `--verification` and `--output` paths to generate and verify the Appendix B tables and figures. Keep private inputs and reference outputs outside the repository.

## Experiment Details

- Experiments 1a and 1b supply belief differences and the factual question.
- Experiments 2a and 2b add the complete frozen interaction.
- Experiments 3a and 3b ask for a verdict rather than an endorsement and follow the permitted categories in their base prompts.

Full articles are not supplied in manager calls. Each call places the own-answer field first, but that same-call answer is exposed to all supplied materials; the optional unaided recall check is the separate memory measure.

The base implementation independently queries both participant orientations: 5 articles × 4 pairs × 5 managers × 2 orientations = **200 calls per family per experiment**. Reports place each orientation beside its counterpart and compare choices by actual participant. These are matched repeated evaluations, not 200 independent training replications.

Requests share a frozen GPU base and LoRA tensors. **Client concurrency** is the maximum number of generation requests the client keeps active at once: the default limit of **8** allows up to eight simultaneous requests, with the rest waiting for a slot. Batches outside the standard input/output profiles use a lower limit of **2** to reduce GPU memory pressure. Token-reservation limits can reduce these counts further; neither number means loading separate copies of the model.

The client records GPU memory, exact request/response text, token IDs, input/output counts, queue time, generation time and batch wall time. Parallel per-call durations overlap; summing them is not elapsed runtime.

## Appendix B analysis code

[Results & Analysis Codes (Appendix B)](Results%20%26%20Analysis%20Codes%20%28Appendix%20B%29/README.md) contains the post-experiment analysis for the final Appendix B exhibits. `Complete_Run_Code.py` runs all eleven scripts; each exhibit also has a standalone entrypoint. This analysis uses externally supplied final experiment outputs, separately from the base-procedure runners in `Experiment Codes`.

The folder covers:

- **Table B1b:** assigned-belief manipulation checks across Mistral Experiments 1a–3a and Qwen Experiments 1b–3b.
- **Table B3 and Figures B3.1–B3.3:** historical debate outcomes, decisions across belief-match configurations, manager/pair heatmaps, and support for participants who retained or revised their answers.
- **Tables B3.4–B3.5 and Figure B3.6:** article-clustered comparisons, within-manager changes across experiments, and support for the participant trained on altered articles by manager beliefs and debate behavior.
- **Figure B3.7 and Tables B3.8–B3.9:** coded reasons in manager explanations, summary patterns, and comparisons between model families.

`requirements.txt` pins the Python libraries, `NUMBERING_MAP.json` records the final exhibit numbering, and `package_manifest.json` verifies the released code files. The folder README documents the private input schema and provides commands for running the whole analysis or a single exhibit. Runs produce table/plot data, LaTeX, figures and local execution checks.

** Public input manifests use `Final Output` aliases and `YOUR PATHWAY` placeholders. Reproduction requires running the experiment first, obtaining the raw data from the experiment by model and experimental conditions, the coding files and templates, and, for the combined runner, the private expected-output references. 

## Reproducibility

`tests/test_offline.py` checks source binding, participant/answer attribution, all 600 base inputs per family, context budgets, stopping logic, recovery and exports without inference. Notebook cells that would train or generate are disabled by default. The port has been checked on CPU; GPU execution of this new repository layout remains a validation step before collecting new experimental data.

Training logs report the checkpoints actually retained. Optimizer states and every intermediate epoch checkpoint were not all retained. Qwen's B checkpoint includes redundant saved tensors; its separate canonical serving export and both hashes are retained. See the training README for the precise lineage and validation selection.

The frozen participant interaction texts and model outputs are research records. A fluent explanation is not itself a correctness measure. Source-based truth, a manager's assigned belief and agreement between participants are separate quantities.

Machine-specific paths are masked with `YOUR PATHWAY`; internal references are relative. No VM hostname, cloud project identifier, credentials or historical run-summary files are included. Model licenses and third-party notices remain applicable. See `Models/README.md` and the upstream model cards.

Active interaction folders, scripts, aliases, notebooks and documentation use **Participant Agent Interaction**. Original source call identifiers and source-file labels inside archived records remain unchanged so the frozen evidence can still be traced to its original hashes.
